SPECIFICATION FOR
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 30 October 1981, after the draft finalized by the Oils and Oilseeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council and Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 UNrDI oil is obtained from seed kernels of UNDI tree (Calophyllum as PUNNAG, SULTAN inophybn Linn.), also variously known CHAMPA, SURPUN, NAMDRU, PUNNA, HONNE, PINNAI, PINNAY, POONAG, DOMBA, POLONG, POON, ALEXANDRIAN LAUREL, LAUREL NUT, etc. UNDI trees grow in coastal districts of Maharashtra, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Orissa, West Bengal and in Andaman Islands. It is also grown as a garden or avenue tree for ornamental purposes. It has sizable potential of availability. 0.3 UNDI kernels are rich in oil having 55 to 75 percent of a green yellow coloured oil with a strong pungent odour. The oil derived from UNDI kernels is suitable for soap-making after proper purification. It is used as a medicinal oil in indigenous systems. It is also used to coat boats to prevent attack from fungus and marine life. 0.4 Oleic acid (35 to 53 percent) and linoleic acid (16 to 29 percent) are the major unsaturated fatty acids present in UNDZ oil. Saturated fatty acids like palmitic acid (15 to 20 percent) and stearic acid (10 to 20 percent) are also present in UNDZ oil, making it suitable for soaps and fatty acids recovery. Due to the presence of lipid associates like calophylloid and inophyllic acid UNDZ oil finds use as a bactericide, anticoagulant and fungicide. 0.5 This standard contains clause 5.1 which between the purchaser and the supplier. calls for an agreement

UNDI OIL

0.6 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from data supplied by Oil Techological Research Institute, Anantapur, Directorate of Oilseeds Development, Hyderabad and Oil Technologists' Association of India. Assistance has also been derived from leaflet No. 3 on non-edible oils published by the erstwhile Indian CentralOilseeds Committee, Hyderabad and the booklet on `Tree-borne Oilseeds' brought out by the Directorate of Non-Edible Oils & Soap Industry of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission, Bombay. Assistance so derived is thankfully acknowledged. 3

MARKING 6.1 The containers shall be marked with the following information: a) Name and type of the material; b) Net mass of the material; c) Manufacturer's name and his recognized trade-mark, if any; d) Batch number or lot number in code or otherwise; land e) Month and year of manufacture. 6.1.1 Mark. The containers may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE - The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer. ISI marked products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

NOTE - `Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.
